question.text:
Let $A$ have eigenvalues $\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\ldots,\lambda_n$ and suppose $P$ diagonalises $A$. Then for any positive integer $k$, $A^k=$
 

  1. $P\begin{bmatrix}
    \lambda_1 & 0 & \cdots & 0\\
    0 & \lambda_2 & \cdots & 0\\
    \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots\\
    0 & 0 & \cdots & \lambda_n
    \end{bmatrix}P^{-1}$

     
  2. $P\begin{bmatrix}
    \lambda_1^k & 0 & \cdots & 0\\
    0 & \lambda_2^k & \cdots & 0\\
    \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots\\
    0 & 0 & \cdots & \lambda_n^k
    \end{bmatrix}P^{-1}$

     
  3. $P^{-1}\begin{bmatrix}
    \lambda_1 & 0 & \cdots & 0\\
    0 & \lambda_2 & \cdots & 0\\
    \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots\\
    0 & 0 & \cdots & \lambda_n
    \end{bmatrix}$

     
  4. None of these.
question.subject: Linear Algebra

question.text:
If $e$ is the rank of matrix $A_{m \times n}$, then rank of matrix $A A^{T}$ is

  1. $e$
     
  2. $m-e$
     
  3. $n-e$
     
  4. $m+n-2 e$
question.subject: Linear Algebra

question.text:
Consider the set of vectors $S=\{v_1,v_2,v_3\}$, where

$$v_1=\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\\2\end{pmatrix}, \qquad
v_2=\begin{pmatrix}2\\1\\1\end{pmatrix}, \qquad
v_3=\begin{pmatrix}t\\1\\t+1\end{pmatrix}$$

and $t$ is a parameter. Which statement is true?

  1. $S$ is a linearly independent set of vectors for all $t$
     
  2. $S$ is a linearly independent set of vectors exactly when $t\ne 4$
     
  3. $S$ is a linearly independent set of vectors exactly when $t=4$
     
  4. $S$ is a linearly independent set of vectors exactly when $t\ne -4$
question.subject: Linear Algebra

question.text:
Let $\mathrm{A}$ be an $\mathrm{n}$ $\times$ $\mathrm{n}$ real matrix for which two distinct non-zero $\mathrm{n}$-dimensional real column vectors $\mathrm{v}_1$ and $\mathrm{v}_2$ satisfy the relation $\mathrm{A}{\mathrm{v}_1} =\mathrm{Av}_2 $.

Which of the folllowing statement(s) about $\mathrm{A}$ is(are) true?

  1. At least one eigenvalue of $\mathrm{A}$ is zero.
     
  2. $\mathrm{A}$ is not full rank.
     
  3. Columns of $\mathrm{A}$ are linearly independent.
     
  4. The determinant of $\mathrm{A}$ is zero.
question.subject: Linear Algebra

question.text:
The Eigen values of a unitary matrix must satisfy the condition that

  1. Always lie inside the unit circle
     
  2. Always lie outside the unit circle
     
  3. Always lie on the unit circle
     
  4. None of these
question.subject: Linear Algebra
